title: The Stalk of Grass 7
content:
A-Qing blinked, caught off guard for a second before stammering, “Y-Yeah! Exactly!”

“Take it easy, then,” Xiao Xingchen said gently. “Don’t rush. You wouldn’t want to crash into someone else.”

He didn’t breathe a word about his own blindness. Taking A-Qing by the hand, he guided her toward the edge of the street. “Walk this way,” he offered softly. “The crowd is thinner.”

Every word and gesture of his was so patient, so tender, that A-Qing’s hand actually hovered in midair, caught in a rare beat of hesitation. But old habits died hard. In the blink of an eye, she skillfully lifted the purse hanging at his waist, flashing an innocent grin: “A-Qing thanks you, Gege!”

“Not ‘Gege,’” Xiao Xingchen corrected gently. “It’s ‘Daozhang’.”

A-Qing fluttered her lashes, playing dumb. “Well, you’re a Daozhang, but you’re still a big brother, aren't you?”

Xiao Xingchen chuckled. “Since you’ve already called me Gege, how about giving Gege’s purse back?”

Even if a street urchin like A-Qing were ten times faster, she was never going to slip past the honed senses of a cultivator. The second she realized she’d been clocked, she gripped her cane, spun on her heel, and bolted. She didn’t even make it two strides before Xiao Xingchen snagged her collar with one hand, hoisting her back like a scruffed kitten. “Didn't I tell you not to run? What if you knock someone over?”

A-Qing squirmed and kicked, her teeth sinking into her lower lip. Uh-oh, Wei Wuxian thought from inside her head. She’s about to scream bloody murder and cry harassment!

Before she could open her lungs, a middle-aged man rounded the street corner in a frantic hurry. The moment his eyes landed on A-Qing, his face lit up with furious triumph. He stormed over, spitting curses: “You little wench, I finally caught you! Cough up my money!”

Cursing wasn't enough to satisfy him; he reared back, swinging a vicious slap straight toward her face. Terrified, A-Qing scrunched her neck and squeezed her eyes shut.

Yet the strike never landed. A pale hand caught the man's wrist midair.

“Peace, friend,” Xiao Xingchen said calmly. “Is it really appropriate to raise your hand against a young girl?”

A-Qing cracked one eye open to peek. The man had put his entire weight into that swing, yet Xiao Xingchen held him back with what looked like effortless grace, not yielding an inch. Intimidated by the cultivator’s quiet strength, the man swallowed his fear and blustered defensively: “Where the hell did you crawl out of, you blind busybody?! Playing the hero, are we? Is this little wildcat your whore or something? She’s a thief, you hear me! She picked my pocket, and since you’re covering for her, you’re no better than a crook yourself!”

Xiao Xingchen kept an iron grip on the man with one hand while holding A-Qing firmly by the scruff with the other. He turned his head toward her. “Return his money.”

Seeing no way out, A-Qing reluctantly fished the meager handful of coins from her tunic and handed them over. Xiao Xingchen released the man, who quickly counted his coin, verified nothing was missing, and eyed the blind cultivator warily. Sensing the man was way out of his league, the brute backed off, slinking away with a sullen scowl.

Xiao Xingchen turned his attention back to the girl. “You’re far too bold. You can’t even see, yet you dare run around picking pockets?”

A-Qing practically bounced in place, bristling with indignation: “He touched me! He pinched my backside, and he pinched it hard! What’s wrong with charging him a little fee? Walking around with a purse that big and barely carrying two coppers to rub together—he has the nerve to throw a tantrum and hit a girl? Broke-ass creep!”

Wei Wuxian couldn't help but marvel internally. You literally threw yourself into his path to rob him blind, and somehow he’s the one at fault? Talk about twisting the narrative.

Xiao Xingchen shook his head, sighing. “If that’s the case, you had even less business provoking him. If no one had stepped in today, a simple slap wouldn't have been the end of it. Take care of yourself, little maiden.”

With that, he turned and began walking in the opposite direction.

Didn’t even ask for his own purse back, Wei Wuxian noted. Turns out this martial uncle of mine has quite the soft spot for the ladies.

A-Qing stood frozen on the street for a moment, clutching the stolen coin pouch in her fist. Suddenly, she shoved it deep into her robes, tapped her bamboo cane against the pavers, and took off after him, barreling straight into Xiao Xingchen’s back.

Xiao Xingchen had to catch her by the shoulders to steady her. “Is there something else?”

A-Qing piped up, “Your money pouch is still with me!”

“Keep it,” Xiao Xingchen replied mildly. “There isn’t much in there anyway. Just promise you won’t steal again until it runs out.”

A-Qing tilted her head. “Hearing that broke creep cussing you out just now... are you actually blind too?”

At her words, the light vanished from Xiao Xingchen’s face, his gentle smile withering instantly.

Nothing cuts deeper than the careless candor of youth. Children speak without filters, and precisely because they don't understand the weight of their words, their strikes land with devastating precision.

Beneath the linen wrapped around his face, a blooming dark stain began to seep through, blood soaking through the cloth. Xiao Xingchen raised a trembling hand, hovering it gingerly over the fabric. The searing, hollow ache of having one's eyes gouged out wasn't something that simply faded with time.

A-Qing, assuming he was merely dizzy, perked up with sudden excitement: “Then I’m coming with you!”

Xiao Xingchen forced a strained, brittle smile. “Why follow me? Do you plan on becoming a Daoist nun?”

“You’re a big blind guy, and I’m a little blind girl,” A-Qing reasoned smoothly. “If we stick together, we can watch each other’s backs! I don’t have parents, and I don't have anywhere to go. Walking with you is no different than wandering alone, so why not?”

She was exceptionally street-smart. Reading his gentle nature like a book, she knew an outright plea might fail, so she tacked on an immediate guilt trip: “If you don’t take me along, I’m going to blow through this money super fast! Once it’s gone, I’ll have to go back to lying and stealing. People will slap me so hard I won't know left from right. Think of how pitiful that’d be!”

Xiao Xingchen couldn’t hold back a chuckle. “Clever little imp. With your quick tongue, you’re the one spinning people in circles. Who on earth could slap you senseless?”

Watching the exchange, Wei Wuxian was struck by a bizarre realization.

Comparing the genuine article with the imposter back in Yi City, Xue Yang’s performance had been downright terrifying in its accuracy! Aside from the physical face, every single tick, cadence, and mannerism was captured so flawlessly that if someone had told him Xue Yang had been possessed by Xiao Xingchen’s ghost, he might have actually bought it.

A-Qing clung to him relentlessly, wheedling, whining, and pulling out every trick in her book. Xiao Xingchen warned her repeatedly that traveling with him was perilous, but she brushed it off like dust. Not even when they passed through a village and he slayed a demonic ox spirit that had terrorized the locals for decades did she flinch. She kept chattering, calling him Daozhang at every turn, sticking to him like stubborn taffy within a three-pace radius. Over time, perhaps charmed by her wit, her courage, and moved by the plight of an orphaned, sightless girl, Xiao Xingchen quietly allowed her to stay by his side.

Wei Wuxian initially assumed Xiao Xingchen had a specific destination in mind. But as the memories flickered forward, tracing the local dialects and terrain revealed a completely erratic path that refused to connect into a logical route. He wasn't heading anywhere; he was simply drifting, night-hunting at random wherever strange rumors or restless spirits called.

Perhaps the horror of the Yueyang Chang Clan crushed him too deeply, Wei Wuxian mused sadly. He lost his taste for the grand sects, yet couldn't bear to abandon his youthful vows. So he chose the life of a wandering rogue, resolving whatever grievances crossed his path, taking it one tragedy at a time.

Presently, Xiao Xingchen and A-Qing were trekking down a flat country road flanked by waist-high weeds. Suddenly, A-Qing let out a sharp cry.

Xiao Xingchen paused instantly. “What happened?”

“Ow! Nothing, just twisted my ankle,” she mumbled.

From her vantage point, Wei Wuxian could tell her ankle was completely fine. If she hadn't been committed to playing the helpless blind girl to keep Xiao Xingchen from leaving her behind, she could have vaulted over the brush like a gazelle. The only reason she’d squeaked was that a casual glance into the tall grass had caught a dark, unmoving silhouette sprawled in the weeds.

Whether the body was dead or alive, trouble was trouble, and A-Qing clearly wanted no part of it. Desperate to steer Xiao Xingchen away, she hurried him along: “Come on, let’s go! Let's find an inn in the next town, I'm completely beat!”

“Didn't you just twist your ankle?” Xiao Xingchen asked gently. “Do you need me to carry you?”

A-Qing beamed, thumping her bamboo cane against the dirt. “Yes, please!”

Smiling, Xiao Xingchen turned his back to her and dropped to one knee, offering a piggyback ride. Just as A-Qing was about to hop on, he raised a hand to hold her back, rising slowly to his feet. His expression hardened. “I smell blood.”

A faint, metallic tang was indeed drifting on the breeze, coming and going with the night wind. Playing dumb, A-Qing sniffled. “Blood? Really? I don't smell anything. Must be some local butcher slaughtering pigs down the road.”

Right on cue, as if fate had a personal vendetta against her, a raspy cough rattled from deep within the brush.

Though it was barely a whisper of a sound, it couldn't slip past Xiao Xingchen’s sharp ears. Locking onto the direction immediately, he stepped into the tall grass and knelt by the fallen figure.

Realizing she couldn't hide it, A-Qing stomped her foot in annoyance, then tapped her cane along, faking her way toward him. “What is it?”

Xiao Xingchen pressed two fingers to the stranger's wrist. “There’s a man lying here.”

“No wonder it smells so bad,” A-Qing grumbled. “Is he dead? Should we dig a hole and bury him?”

Dead people couldn't cause trouble, so A-Qing was practically praying the stranger was a corpse.

“Not yet,” Xiao Xingchen corrected. “He’s severely injured, but still breathing.”

Without hesitating, he gently scooped the bleeding stranger onto his back.

Seeing her piggyback ride stolen by a foul, blood-soaked stray, A-Qing pouted, furiously jabbing her cane into the dirt until she’d punched several deep holes into the ground. Still, knowing Xiao Xingchen’s bottomless compassion, she kept her complaints to herself.

They returned to the road and kept walking. The longer they trudged, the more an eerie familiarity gnawed at Wei Wuxian. Wait... isn't this the exact road Lan Zhan and I took into Yi City?

Sure enough, a towering city gate loomed at the end of the avenue.

Back then, the city wasn't this hollow ruin. The watchtowers stood intact, and the ancient stone walls were free of graffiti. Passing through the gates, the mist hung slightly thicker than in the countryside, but compared to the supernatural, suffocating smog that would later blanket the city, it was barely noticeable. Warm lantern light spilled from windows along the street, carrying the muffled hum of conversation. It was quiet, but undeniably alive.

Knowing no respectable inn would open its doors to a stranger drenched in blood, Xiao Xingchen didn't bother looking for lodging. Instead, he flagged down a passing night watchman to ask if there was an empty mortuary nearby.

“There’s one down that way,” the watchman offered. “The old caretaker passed away just last month, so the place is sitting abandoned.” Seeing that Xiao Xingchen was blind, the kindly watchman took pity on him and guided them over personally.

It was the very same mortuary where Xiao Xingchen’s corpse would one day rest.

Thanking the watchman, Xiao Xingchen carried the wounded man into the side room on the right. The quarters were modest: a low cot tucked against the wall, alongside a full set of battered cookware. He laid the man down with great care, retrieved a medicinal pill from his Qiankun pouch, and eased it past the stranger's tightly clenched teeth.

A-Qing poked around the dark room, calling out in delight, “There’s so much stuff in here! I found a basin!”

“Is there a stove?” Xiao Xingchen asked.

“Yep!”

“A-Qing, see if you can boil some hot water. Be careful not to burn yourself.”

A-Qing made a face, but set to work anyway. Xiao Xingchen checked the man's burning forehead and administered a second elixir.

Wei Wuxian was dying to get a good look at the stranger's face, but A-Qing found the man utterly repulsive and refused to spare him a single glance. Once the water boiled, Xiao Xingchen dipped a cloth and gently dabbed away the layers of crusted blood from the man's features. Curiosity finally getting the better of her, A-Qing stole a peek—and let out a quiet, surprised gasp.

Cleaned up, the bastard was actually quite handsome.

Taking in the boyish face, Wei Wuxian’s heart plummeted straight to his boots.

It was Xue Yang.

What a twisted, cruel joke, Wei Wuxian thought grimly. Xiao Xingchen... you truly have the worst luck in the world.

At this point in time, Xue Yang was barely past boyhood—seven parts roguish charm, three parts childish innocence. Who could have guessed that a kid with such a sweet, dimpled grin could be an unhinged butcher capable of wiping out entire bloodlines?

Doing the mental math, this had to be shortly after Jin Guangyao ascended to the seat of Chief Cultivator. Xue Yang’s battered state meant he had likely just barely survived Jin Guangyao’s purge. Having failed to finish him off, Jin Guangyao naturally kept quiet about the botched hit—or perhaps assumed Xue Yang was as good as dead from his wounds, publicly announcing the rogue had been dealt with. Yet vile pests had a habit of clinging to life. On the brink of death, Xue Yang had been scooped up from the roadside by none other than his mortal nemesis.

Tragically, it would never occur to Xiao Xingchen to map this stranger's face with his hands. By a sick twist of fate, he had rescued the very monster who had destroyed his life. And while A-Qing had eyes, she knew nothing of the cultivation world, nothing of Xue Yang, and nothing of their bloody feud. Hell, she didn't even know Xiao Xingchen’s real name...

Wei Wuxian could only sigh. You couldn't write worse luck if you tried. It was as if all the misfortune under heaven had converged entirely on this one man.

On the cot, Xue Yang’s brows twitched. Feeling him stir as he tended to the wounds, Xiao Xingchen warned softly, “Don’t move.”

A criminal like Xue Yang lived with his guard permanently raised. The instant the voice registered, his eyes snapped open. He bolted upright, scrambling back into the corner of the wall like a cornered viper, his eyes burning with feral, predatory malice. It was the gaze of a trapped beast, dripping with naked cruelty, sending an icy prickle of dread straight through A-Qing’s scalp.

The chill shot through Wei Wuxian as well, screaming in his head: Say something! Speak! Xiao Xingchen could never forget your voice!

Xue Yang rasped, “You...”

The moment the syllable scraped past his lips, Wei Wuxian felt a cold dread settle in. Even speaking wouldn't help.

Xue Yang’s throat was torn up from internal bleeding. After coughing up rivers of blood, his voice was a ruined, gravelly rasp, completely unrecognizable.

Xiao Xingchen remained sitting calmly by the bedside. “I told you not to move; your wounds will reopen. Relax. I brought you back to treat you—I mean you no harm.”

Xue Yang’s mind worked with terrifying speed. Realizing Xiao Xingchen hadn't recognized him, his eyes darted around, coughing faintly as he tested the waters: “Who are you?”

A-Qing chimed in with a huff, “Got eyes, don't you? Look for yourself—he's a wandering Daoist! He busted his back hauling you all the way here to patch you up with precious spirit elixirs, and you're glaring at him like that?!”

Xue Yang’s gaze snapped toward her, his tone dropping cold. “A blind girl?”

Damn it, Wei Wuxian cursed internally.

The little bastard was too sharp, too paranoid. Even with A-Qing sporting milky-white eyes, he didn't let his guard down for a second, hunting for any slip-up. Xue Yang had only spoken four words, and from tone alone, it was impossible to deduce whether he had been glaring—unless someone had actually seen his face.

Fortunately, A-Qing had spent her entire life spinning lies. She fired back without missing a beat: “What, looking down on blind folk? It took a couple of blind people to pull you out of the ditch, otherwise you’d be rotting meat by the roadside! Not even a ‘thank you’ for the Daozhang, no manners at all! Calling me a blind girl right to my face... what’s wrong with being blind anyway...?!”

She pivoted effortlessly, playing the part of an aggrieved, petulant child, muttering sulky complaints under her breath. Xiao Xingchen hurried to console her, while Xue Yang leaned his head against the plaster wall, rolling his eyes in silent annoyance.

Turning back to the cot, Xiao Xingchen chided gently, “Don’t press your back against the cold wall. I haven't finished bandaging your leg yet—come here.”

Xue Yang stayed expressionless, weighing his options.

Xiao Xingchen added, “If you delay treatment any longer, you risk crippling the limb.”

That settled it.

Wei Wuxian could see the gears turning in Xue Yang's head: he was crippled with injuries and completely helpless. Without medical care, he was a dead man. Since Xiao Xingchen was foolish enough to play the selfless saint, why not milk the idiot for all he was worth?

His expression flipped in an instant, dripping with humble gratitude: “Then I shall trouble you, Daozhang.”

Watching Xue Yang switch masks on a dime, Wei Wuxian broke out in a cold sweat for the two people in the room—one truly blind, one faking it. Especially A-Qing. She saw everything. If Xue Yang ever caught wind of the fact that she wasn't actually blind, he would slit her throat without hesitation to protect his identity. Even knowing A-Qing had ultimately met a tragic end at his hands, living through the dread firsthand was nerve-wracking.

Suddenly, Wei Wuxian noticed something: Xue Yang was carefully, deliberately keeping his left hand tucked out of sight, ensuring Xiao Xingchen’s fingers never brushed it. Leaning in closer, Wei Wuxian saw why: the little finger on Xue Yang’s left hand was sheared clean off. The scar was old, meaning Xiao Xingchen definitely knew the notorious villain possessed only nine fingers.

No wonder he wore a black leather glove when masquerading as the Daoist in Yi City.

Xiao Xingchen tended to the wounds with meticulous care, wrapping the linen in clean, immaculate layers. “All done,” he said, rising. “Try to keep still, or the bone will set crooked.”

Convinced that Xiao Xingchen was genuinely clueless, that trademark lazy smirk crept back onto Xue Yang’s face despite his battered state. “Doesn't the Daozhang care to ask who I am? Or how I ended up so badly injured?”

Anyone else in his shoes would have avoided the topic like poison to prevent slipping up, yet he boldly poked the bear on purpose.

Xiao Xingchen gathered his medicine box and clean bandages, his tone warm and even: “If you do not offer it, why should I pry? A chance meeting by the wayside, a simple helping hand—it cost me nothing, and once your wounds heal, our paths will part naturally. Were I in your position, there are things in my past I would rather leave unsaid as well.”

Even if you asked, Wei Wuxian thought dryly, that little sociopath would spin a sob story so seamless it’d make your head spin. Xiao Xingchen’s restraint was born of pure nobility and respect, but Xue Yang was the kind of monster who weaponized basic human decency against you. Wei Wuxian was dead certain: not only was Xue Yang going to milk Xiao Xingchen for free medical care, but once his legs healed, he wasn't going to "part paths" anywhere!

While Xue Yang rested in the side room, Xiao Xingchen stepped out into the mortuary’s main hall. Finding an empty casket, he swept up armfuls of dry straw from the floor and layered the bottom thick. Turning to A-Qing, he said gently, “The man inside is badly hurt, so I’ve given him the cot. I must ask you to make do sleeping in here. The straw is fresh; it shouldn't be cold.”

Having spent her life sleeping in gutters and alleyways, A-Qing didn't care in the slightest. “What’s there to complain about? A roof over my head is plenty! It’s warm enough, so don’t you dare try giving me your outer robe again.”

Xiao Xingchen patted her head with a smile, tucked his horsehair whisk into his belt, strapped his sword to his back, and stepped out into the night. For her safety, he never permitted her to tag along on his night-hunts.

A-Qing climbed into the casket, settling into the straw. She had barely shut her eyes when Xue Yang’s voice drifted through the wooden partition: “Hey, little blind girl. Come over here.”

A-Qing poked her head over the rim. “What do you want?”

“Got some candy for you.”

A-Qing’s mouth watered involuntarily, but she snapped, “Don't want it! Not coming!”

Xue Yang’s voice adopted a syrupy, threatening purr: “Sure about that? Are you hiding because you're scared of me? Do you honestly think that just because I'm on this bed, I can't drag myself over there and find you?”

The chilling edge in his tone sent a shiver down A-Qing’s spine. Imagining that smiling, vicious face suddenly leaning over the edge of her coffin was terrifying enough that she grabbed her bamboo stick and reluctantly shuffled toward the side room, tapping the floorboards with calculated hesitation.

Before she could speak, a small object whistled through the dark straight at her face!

Wei Wuxian instinctively braced to dodge, terrified it was a concealed projectile, though he had zero control over the vessel. In the same breath, realization struck him like cold water: A trap!

Xue Yang was testing her. A truly blind person would never flinch from something they couldn't see!

A-Qing proved herself a seasoned master of deception. Spotting the flying object, she didn't blink, duck, or twitch, letting the candy bounce squarely off her collarbone. Only then did she jump back with a theatrical shriek: “Hey! What the hell did you throw at me?!”

Having failed to trip her up, Xue Yang drawled, “Candy, obviously. A treat. Forgot you couldn't see to catch it—it’s down by your feet.”

A-Qing scowled, dropped to a crouch, and made a convincing show of blindly patting the floor until her fingers found the small, paper-wrapped sweet. Having never tasted candy before, she swallowed her pride, dusted it off on her sleeve, and popped it into her mouth, crunching away with noisy delight.

Xue Yang lay propped on one elbow, smirking lazily. “Good, isn't it, little blind girl?”

“I have a name,” she spat around the sugar. “Stop calling me that.”

“You haven't told me your name, so what else am I supposed to call you?”

A-Qing only ever gave her name to people she liked, but hating his pet name even more, she relented: “Listen up: my name is A-Qing. Don't you dare call me ‘little blind girl’ ever again!” Realizing she’d sounded a bit too aggressive, she hastily redirected, wanting to soothe the psychopath: “You’re weird, you know that? Bleeding out and half-dead, but you still carry candy around?”

Xue Yang let out a soft laugh. “When I was a kid, I loved sweets, but I could never have any. I’d watch other kids eat them until my mouth watered. So I promised myself: if I ever made it big, I’d carry all the candy in the world on me every single day.”

Having finished the piece, A-Qing licked her lips, her sweet tooth easily winning out over her disgust. “Got any more?”

Xue Yang smiled. “Of course. Come closer, and I’ll give it to you.”

A-Qing pushed herself up, tapping her stick across the floor toward the bed.

Halfway across the room, Xue Yang’s smile remained pleasant, yet an eerie, lethal glint flashed behind his eyes. Silently, smoothly, the dark steel of a longsword slid from beneath his sleeve.

Jiangzai.

He aimed the tip straight at A-Qing’s stomach. Two more steps, and she would impale herself on the blade. But if she hesitated for even a fraction of a second, her sight would be exposed!

Sharing her senses, Wei Wuxian felt the hair on the back of her neck stand on end. Yet the girl possessed nerves of absolute steel. Without breaking her blank, shuffling stride, she continued feeling her way forward. Sure enough, the moment the blade hovered barely half an inch from her tunic, Xue Yang pulled his hand back, sliding Jiangzai back into his cuff. In its place, he produced two pieces of candy—tossing one to A-Qing and flicking the other into his own mouth.

“Hey, A-Qing,” he murmured, chewing lazily. “Where does that Daozhang of yours run off to in the middle of the night?”

Licking her treat, A-Qing mumbled, “Hunting, I think.”

Xue Yang scoffed. “Hunting? You mean night-hunting.”

“Whatever, hunting, night-hunting—it’s all the same thing,” she waved off. “Running around slaying ghosts and monsters for people without charging a single copper.”

Inside her head, Wei Wuxian mentally applauded. Brilliant.

She hadn't forgotten the term; she remembered every single word Xiao Xingchen had ever spoken. She had deliberately fumbled the phrase to bait Xue Yang into correcting her—forcing him to subtly admit his familiarity with the cultivation world. Xue Yang had tried to test her, only to get played right back. For such a young girl, her instincts were terrifyingly sharp.

Xue Yang sneered, though genuine curiosity tinged his voice: “He’s blind. Can he even night-hunt?”

A-Qing flared up. “There you go again! So what if he’s blind?! Even without his eyes, the Daozhang is incredible! His sword goes whoosh whoosh whoosh—fast as lightning!”

Midway through her animated pantomime, Xue Yang cut in softly: “If you can’t see, how do you know his sword is fast?”

A lethal trap, dismantled in a heartbeat. A-Qing immediately threw a childish tantrum: “I said it’s fast, so it’s fast! His sword is definitely fast! Even if I can't see it, do you think I'm deaf?! What is your problem anyway, always looking down on blind people?!”

She sounded like nothing more than a starry-eyed, stubborn little girl blindly hyping up her hero—utterly, disarmingly natural.

Three tests, three dead ends. The suspicion on Xue Yang’s face finally melted away, fully convinced she was blind.

A-Qing, however, was on high alert. The following afternoon, when Xiao Xingchen returned with spare lumber, thatch, and tiles to patch the leaking roof, she pulled him outside by his sleeve. She whispered frantically for several minutes, warning him that this stranger was shady, practiced cultivation, hid his background, and definitely wasn't a good person. Unfortunately, assuming the missing pinky was just an irrelevant detail, she never mentioned the dead giveaway.

Xiao Xingchen patted her head, gently reassuring her: “You already ate his candy, so stop trying to run him out. Once his injuries heal, he will leave on his own. No one wants to linger in a dreary place like this.”

He wasn't wrong. The mortuary had only one bed, and if rain ever blew in, the rotting roof would make their lives miserable. Nobody sane would choose to stay.

A-Qing opened her mouth to argue further, but a drawling voice drifted from behind them: “Talking about me?”

He had actually limped out of bed. Without missing a beat, A-Qing sneered, “Who’s talking about you? Don't flatter yourself!” Tapping her cane loudly, she ducked back inside and huddled beneath the window to eavesdrop.

Outside, Xiao Xingchen frowned. “Your wounds are fresh. Wandering around like this isn't wise.”

“Moving around helps me heal faster,” Xue Yang said casually. “Besides, it's not like both my legs are broken. I’m used to cuts like this; I grew up taking beatings.”

Unsure whether to comfort him or laugh it off as a joke, Xiao Xingchen paused before offering a quiet, sympathetic “Ah...”

Xue Yang pressed on, “Daozhang, you hauled all these materials back—planning on patching the roof?”

“Mm. We will be staying here for a while, and a broken roof makes for poor shelter, neither good for your recovery nor A-Qing’s comfort.”

“Need a hand?”

Xiao Xingchen dipped his head. “No need to trouble yourself.”

“Do you actually know how to do it?”

Xiao Xingchen gave a sheepish, self-deprecating laugh. “To be completely honest, I have never tried.”

And so, the two of them set to work—one providing the manual labor, the other offering pointers. Xue Yang had a silver tongue, cracking witty jokes with a roguish, streetwise edge. Having spent his youth in secluded cultivation, Xiao Xingchen was entirely unaccustomed to that brand of crude banter and couldn't help laughing at every few quips. Under the window, A-Qing listened to their cheerful chatter, silently mouthing through her teeth: I hope a falling tile crushes your rotten skull.

Wei Wuxian shared every bit of her loathing.

Xue Yang had been beaten within an inch of his life, a feud tied directly to old grudges involving Xiao Xingchen. Deep down, the psychopath probably dreamed of hacking Xiao Xingchen into a bloody pulp, yet here he was, casually shooting the breeze like an old pal. If Wei Wuxian were in his own body, he’d have slit Xue Yang’s throat right through the window to snuff out the disaster before it started. But he was just a passenger in A-Qing's memories, and the girl was utterly powerless.

Roughly a month later, nursed by Xiao Xingchen’s tireless care, Xue Yang’s wounds had mostly healed. Aside from a lingering limp in his stride, he was as good as new. Yet he never breathed a word about leaving, continuing to crowd into the dilapidated mortuary with the other two, scheming who-knew-what.

One evening, after tucking A-Qing into her straw-filled casket, Xiao Xingchen prepared to set out on another night-hunt.

Xue Yang’s voice piped up from the cot: “Daozhang, how about taking me along tonight?”

His ruined vocal cords had long since recovered, but he deliberately maintained the altered, gravelly tone to hide his real voice.

Xiao Xingchen smiled. “I’m afraid not. Every time you open your mouth, you make me laugh. And when I laugh, my sword arm wavers.”

Xue Yang whined with exaggerated, pitiful puppy eyes, “I won't say a word, I swear! I'll carry your sword, I'll run your errands—don't leave me behind.”

He was a master at playing the clingy younger brother. Having raised junior disciples during his years under Baoshan Sanren, Xiao Xingchen naturally treated him like a younger peer. Knowing the young man also dabbled in cultivation, he relented with a warm nod.

Xue Yang tagging along out of the goodness of his heart? Not a chance, Wei Wuxian thought sharply. If A-Qing doesn't follow them, we're going to miss the crucial piece.

A-Qing was far too clever to let them walk off alone, knowing Xue Yang was up to no good. The second the front door shut, she scrambled out of the coffin, trailing them through the dark. Terrified of being spotted, she kept a wide distance; between her caution and their cultivator footwork, she lost their trail before long.

Fortunately, Xiao Xingchen had mentioned while washing vegetables earlier that a nearby hamlet was suffering from walking corpses, warning them not to wander off. Remembering the village's direction, A-Qing sprinted toward the settlement. Squeezing through a dog-hole beneath the perimeter fence, she hid behind the corner of an old farmhouse and peeked out.

Whether A-Qing fully understood what she was looking at was unclear, but the sight struck Wei Wuxian with an immediate, paralyzing chill.

Xue Yang was leaning against a roadside wall, arms crossed, his head tilted in an easy, pleasant smile.

Standing opposite him was Xiao Xingchen, his blade drawn with serene, unhurried grace. Shuanghua cut through the air in a flash of pristine silver, driving clean through the heart of a villager.

That villager was a living human being.
